headline: Voters reject data center development across 2026 midterm ballots
summary: Outlets report that US voters broadly rejected data-center development in the November 2026 midterms, with Ohio's rebuke cited as especially strong and the opposition described as crossing party lines. They disagree on the exact count of data-center ballot measures, citing either 45 or 41, while Big Tech calls the backlash anti-Trump rather than anti-tech sentiment.

claims.statement: US voters broadly rejected data-center development in the 2026 midterm elections.

sources.quote: Americans overwhelmingly voted against data centers in the midterms
The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers
Tech industry in denial as US overwhelmingly votes to restrict AI, data centers.

claims.statement: Tomshardware reports 45 data-center-related measures were put on the midterm ballot.
Techcrunch reports 41 data-center-related measures were voted on in the midterms.
Big Tech has characterized the backlash as anti-Trump sentiment rather than opposition to tech itself.

sources.quote: Big Tech claims voters’ AI backlash is “anti-Trump” not “anti-tech”

claims.statement: Opposition to data centers in the midterms crossed party lines.

sources.quote: Data center opposition crossed party lines in Tuesday’s midterms.

claims.statement: The rebuke against data centers was especially strong in Ohio.

sources.quote: Nowhere was the rebuke stronger than the now-blue Ohio.

discrepancies.explanation: Outlets differ on how many data-center-related measures appeared on midterm ballots: tomshardware says 45, techcrunch says 41.
